newsitem.title: USA: Mercedes-Benz U.S. sales up 18.4 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes-Benz U.S. sales up 18.4 pct in 1996.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz of North America Inc on Monday that its 1996 year-end sales totaled 90,844 vehicles, an increase of 18.4 percent over the 76,752 vehicles sold in 1995.
The 1996 total represents the highest annual sales volume for Mercedes-Benz since 1986, when the company sold 99,314 vehicles.
Mercedes is a unit of Daimler-Benz AG.
Earlier, Mercedes executives said the German luxury car marker expects to sell more than 100,000 vehicles in the United States for the first time in 1997.

"No doubt 1996 has been an incredible year for us -- the second best in our history, in fact," Michael Bassermann, president of Mercedes-Benz North America Inc, said in a statement released from the North American International Auto Show here.
"We've worked extremely hard the last few years to reshape our organization with stylish products, which have a lot of emotional appeal and offer tremendous value," he added.

Sales for the year were led by Mercedes' E-Class with sales of 37,956 vehicles, up 52.3 percent from the 24,915 the previous year. There have been nearly 40,000 new E-class cars sold in the United States since their introduction in November 1995.

For the month of December, Mercedes-Benz sold 8,552 vehicles, an increase of 1.1 percent over the 8,455 sold in December 1995. Leading the way for the month was the C-Class, with sales of 2,732, an increase of 19 percent over the 2,296 vehicles sold in December 1995.
